- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or 0.5–1.5 price points.
- Model consistently over-forecasts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85–90), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5 price point lag correction for next 7 days.
- When sentiment is low (0.00) and history shows volatility, model underreacts; increase forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 5 days to capture surprise moves.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 90% of 30-day mean by day 10–15, model often overestimates; cap forecast at 95% of mean + 2x standard deviation.
